mechanism: Foscarnet causes electrolyte disturbances (hypocalcemia, hypomagnesemia) and can impair renal function, while enalapril increases potassium retention and is renally cleared, increasing risk of hyperkalemia and enalapril accumulation.
action: Monitor serum electrolytes (potassium, calcium, magnesium), renal function, and blood pressure closely; adjust enalapril dose if renal function declines; consider alternative antihypertensive if significant electrolyte abnormalities develop.
